<!-- pr-reviewer: 5d112cc6c77442eb2341b2359b19c9b935b0d849 -->
Ready for the maintainer to merge.

What looks good
- The two new rows ("The part is" = Cut-off piece, "Back stock" = 0) match the UI labels and defaults in `crates/ui/src/egui_app/turning_page.rs` (lines 298-314) and `crates/motion/src/turning/parting_law.rs` (the `PartKept::CutOff` default, and the `PartKerf` default `back_stock` of 0).
- The prose is true to the code: the whole kerf stays on the scrap side (`flank()` moves the flank into the scrap side at line 118-124), and zero back stock puts the blade's flank on the plane.
- The new decision file follows the `docs/decisions/` README format (heading, Decision, Why, Dropped, Cost to change later) and records nothing beyond the guide change.
- The adjacent turning sections have no other Part settings table with this gap.

What was checked
- The full diff: 2 files, both docs. No code, no process files, no `.github/`, `build.rs`, scripts, `xtask/`, `Cargo.toml`, `AGENTS.md`, snapshots or goldens. No build or gate was run, by design: this is a documentation-only change.
- Trial merge with main (origin/main `267ee509...`): already up to date, no conflicts.
- `git diff --check`: clean (the contributor also reported it).
- Issue #3680 asked for exactly this change: the two rows, the same wording, and a check of the neighbouring turning sections.

Verification by the contributor (noted, not re-run for a docs-only PR)
- Focused doc assertions failed on the base and passed with this change.
- `cargo xtask gate quick --base origin/main`: exit 0, zero steps.
- GuideIcons passed. OperationReferencePictures failed on the unchanged RotaryFlow gap, at the same enum comparison on the base - a pre-existing baseline failure, not a blocker here.

Requested before merge
- Nothing. No blocking findings.

Notes
- Zola is not installed in this environment, so site rendering is untested. That is consistent with the contributor's stated limits.
- One nuance the prose gets right but could make even sharper: "Back stock moves the whole kerf away from the parting plane" - the code moves the flank (and so the whole kerf) into the scrap side, not the part side. The wording is accurate; a reader of the code will see it in `flank()`.

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.
